Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}

        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."

If you acquired a business with employees, you have the option of keeping the previous owner's UI tax rate.\nuser: I do not agree with my UI rate, I want to protest my UI rate, please.\nassistant: You can protest your UI rates from the DE 2088 or benefit charges on the DE 428T online or by mail. To protest your UI rate online, you can follow these steps:\n1. Log in to e-Services for Business.\n2. Select 'Show More' from the Account Management panel.\n3. Select 'Protest UI Rate'.\n4. Enter the required information and submit.\nAfter you submit this information, you will receive a confirmation number. \nIf you prefer to protest by mail, you can include your EDD employer payroll tax account number, the items you want to protest, the reason for protesting, and mail your written protest to: Employment Development DepartmentRate Management Group, MIC 4PO Box 826880Sacramento, CA 94280-0001. Please note that protests with missing or incorrect information will be returned.\nuser: what is Benefit Charges, please? Can I protest Benefit Charges as well?",

For good cause, you may request an extension of up to **60 days**, but the request must be submitted **in writing before the protest deadline**. [S10]\n\nProtests are reviewed on the facts of each case. You will receive a determination by mail; if denied, you will receive an explanation and information about your petition rights. [S11]"
}
